paper_metadata.title: Microstructure and mechanical properties of a novel Nb–V–Ce multi-microalloyed low-alloy cast steel

evidence.quote: a small amount of V is integrated into M23C6 in 0.3Si–0.04Nb–0.05V steel (Fig. 5d, k). This suggests that V will co-precipitate with other elements as M23C6
a certain amount of Nb-rich precipitate is observed in 0.3Si–0.04Nb–0.05V steel, with size ranging from 50 to 100 nm (Fig. 5g–i, m). Crystal structure analysis conﬁrms this precipitate as NbC
In 0.6Si–0Nb–0V steel, elongated MnS inclusions were predominant, accompanied by a minor presence of Al2O3, ranging in size from 30 to 50 lm (Fig. 9a)
In 0.6Si–0Nb–0V steel, elongated MnS inclusions were predominant, accompanied by a minor presence of Al2O3, ranging in size from 30 to 50 lm (Fig. 9a)
the inclusions in 0.3Si–0.04Nb–0.05 V steel were predominantly spherical composite inclusions of MnS–CexAlyOz–CexSy–CexOySz, with sizes smaller than 5 lm (Fig. 9b)
it is plausible that the spherical inclusions post-composite microalloying may represent a MnS–CeAlO3–Ce2S3–Ce2O2S composite phase
as Si content decreases, martensite transforms toward equiaxed morphology, highlighting the notable impact of Si content variation on the phase transformation of the matrix
this is consistent with the experimental results, which show that after multi-microalloyed treatment, the grain size is signiﬁcantly reﬁned (Fig. 2a–c)
